'''Patrick David Gallagher''' (born March 29, 1963) is an American physicist and former chancellor of the [[University of Pittsburgh]]. He previously served as acting [[United States Deputy Secretary of Commerce|United States deputy secretary of commerce]] from 2013 to 2014 and 14th director of the [[National Institute of Standards and Technology]] from 2009 and 2014.

Following his resignation from the chancellor position at Pitt in 2023, he joined the university's Department of Physics and Astronomy.

==Biography==

Gallagher was born and raised in [[Albuquerque]] to Claire A. Gallagher (née Selter; born in [[Sunbury, PA]] to Agnes J. Selter (née Karb) and Adolf P. Selter) and John Gallagher (born in [[Ireland]], having moved to [[Philadelphia]] at the age of 2).<ref>{{cite web |title=Patrick Gallagher's Pittsburgh Roots |url=http://www.news.pitt.edu/chancellorelect/pittsburgh |website=[[University of Pittsburgh]] |accessdate=December 14, 2017}}</ref> His father, worked at [[Sandia National Laboratories]]. During high school, the young Gallagher spent summers working on public health and sanitation projects in Mexico, Ecuador, and Honduras under sponsorship of [[Amigos de las Américas]]. He graduated from St. Pius High School.

Gallagher studied Physics and Philosophy at [[Benedictine College]] in Atchison, Kansas. After graduating in 1985, he taught math and science for a year at [[Bishop LeBlond High School]] in St. Joseph, Missouri, where he also served as head coach for the cross-country track team. Returning to graduate school, he received his Ph.D. in physics at the [[University of Pittsburgh]] in 1991,<ref name="thesis-gallagher-1991">{{cite thesis |url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/303948875/ |title=The interaction of colloidal polystyrene latex spheres with a critical binary liquid mixture |date=1991 |publisher=[[University of Pittsburgh]] |type=Ph.D. |last=Gallagher |first=Patrick David |id={{ProQuest|303948875}} |url-access=subscription }}</ref> and did post-doctoral research at [[Boston University]]. He joined the NIST Center for Neutron Research as an instrumental scientist in 1993. His research interests have included neutron and X-ray instrumentation and studies of soft condensed matter systems such as liquids, polymers, and gels.<ref>AllGov, [http://www.allgov.com/officials/gallagher-patrick?officialid=29181 "Gallagher, Patrick"]</ref>

In 2000, Gallagher was selected as NIST agency representative at the [[National Science and Technology Council]] (NSTC). Then, starting in 2004, he served for four years as director of the NIST Center for Neutron Research (NCNR), a national user facility for neutron scattering on the NIST Gaithersburg campus. In 2008, he became deputy director of NIST.<ref name="nist">NIST, [https://www.nist.gov/director/bios/gallagher.cfm "Patrick D. Gallagher"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140924063026/http://www.nist.gov/director/bios/gallagher.cfm |date=September 24, 2014 }}</ref><ref>Political Appointee Project, [http://www.politicalappointeeproject.org/profile/patrick-d-gallagher "Director, NIST"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140224092438/http://www.politicalappointeeproject.org/profile/patrick-d-gallagher |date=February 24, 2014 }}</ref>

Nominated by President Obama, Gallagher was confirmed as the 14th Director of NIST on November 5, 2009. He also served as [[Under Secretary of Commerce for Standards and Technology]], a new position created in the [[America COMPETES Act|America COMPETES Reauthorization Act]] of 2010, signed by President Obama on January 4, 2011.

Gallagher was the 18th Chancellor of the University of Pittsburgh, where he served from 2014 through 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |title=University of Pittsburgh Former Chancellor website. |url=https://www.former-chancellor-gallagher.pitt.edu/about-chancellor-gallagher |access-date=2024-06-03 |website=www.former-chancellor-gallagher.pitt.edu}}</ref>

Gallagher has been active in the area of U.S. policy for scientific user facilities and was chair of the Interagency Working Group on neutron and light source facilities under the [[Office of Science and Technology Policy]]. Currently, he serves as co-chair of the Standards Subcommittee under the White House [[National Science and Technology Council]].<ref name="nist" />

Gallagher and his wife, Karen Jane (Abrahamson) Gallagher, an occupational therapist, have three sons, Sean, Devin, and Ryan.<ref>[http://www.gpo.gov/fdsys/pkg/CHRG-111shrg55981/pdf/CHRG-111shrg55981.pdf "Hearing before the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation, United States Senate"] (October 15, 2009)</ref>

==Honors==
On June 23, 2023, the University of Pittsburgh announced that the plaza and walkway outside the 5th Avenue entrance of the [[William Pitt Union]] would be named in honor of Gallagher's service as chancellor of the university.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.utimes.pitt.edu/news/trustees-honor-gallagher|title=Trustees Honor Gallagher, Cudd at Their Last Meeting as Pitt's Leaders|date=June 26, 2023|first=Susan|last=Jones|newspaper=University Times|volume=55|issue=22|accessdate=October 1, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://triblive.com/news/pennsylvania/walk-or-run-this-busy-spot-on-the-university-of-pittsburgh-campus-has-a-new-name/|title=Walk or run, this busy spot on Pitt campus has a new name|first=Bill|last=Schackner|newspaper=Pittsburgh Tribune-Review|date=June 23, 2023|accessdate=October 1, 2024}}</ref>
